quotes.why: The same opponent in Chökyi Gyaltsen's own mtha' dpyod, stated in full: both halves of the thesis (cause refuge and result refuge) are given, which the spyi don abbreviates to the first half only.

The mtha' dpyod grounds 'every Buddha is of one continuum with the path-of-accumulation bodhisattva' in the fact that every Buddha was preceded by that bodhisattva's realization — a different and more direct reason than the spyi don's appeal to sentient beings.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། same passage, the converse argument
quotes.why: The converse half of the proof, from the bodhisattva's side: a bodhisattva is one continuum with the Buddha because Buddhahood is its own final attainment — which is why 'one continuum' here tracks the relation of seeker to goal.

In the mtha' dpyod the premise the spyi don uses as its final reason — 'whatever is a sentient being is one continuum with the Buddha' — appears as an opponent's attempted absurdity, which Chökyi Gyaltsen accepts before blocking the next step with 'not pervaded': the spyi don's p393 is this same exchange.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་གཉིས་པའི་མཐའ་དཔྱོད། on whether all sentient beings will become Buddhas. Found by direct search.
quotes.why: Chökyi Gyaltsen elsewhere grounding the claim that all sentient beings will become Buddhas in a type (རིགས) that can become one — the ground the paragraph's last reason leaves unstated.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04024_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, Ratnagotravibhāga (རྒྱུད་བླ་མ།), Tengyur D4024, the three reasons for the buddha-nature of beings. Found by direct search.
quotes.why: The canonical source for the doctrine the paragraph's last reason depends on — every embodied being has the buddha-nature because the lineage exists — cited here from Maitreya's root text, not from a commentary that repeats it. The paragraph does not quote it.

quotes.citation: སྐབས་དང་པོའི་སྤྱི་དོན། p390, the own-system reading of the Ratnagotravibhāga refuge verse. Found by direct search.
quotes.why: This text's own positive statement, two paragraphs earlier: the cause refuge is the Buddha already accomplished in another's continuum — the wording the opponent of p392 hardens into 'of a different continuum'.

Gyaltsab Je's sentence, which the spyi don's p390 follows almost word for word under the same heading: he calls the cause refuge simply the Buddha 'already accomplished', with no mention of continuum at all.

quotes.file: Tengyur/06 SEMS TZAM_Mind Only School (Cittamātra)/VOL 1 (PHI)/TD04024_THEG PA CHEN PO RGYUD BLA MA'I BSTAN BCOS (Mahāyānottara Tantra Śāstra)_unicode.txt
quotes.citation: Maitreya, Ratnagotravibhāga (རྒྱུད་བླ་མ།), Tengyur D4024, chapter on the Three Jewels. Found by direct search.
quotes.why: The root verse the whole 'general presentation of refuge' glosses, and on which the cause/result distinction is hung; cited from the canonical text, which reads བསླབ་དོན where the yig cha at p390 has སློབ་དོན.

quotes.citation: ལུང་རིགས་ཀྱི་རོལ་མཚོ། on the Ornament's instruction on the Three Jewels, reconciling the Ornament with the sūtras
quotes.why: An early Kadam-period text using 'the Three Jewels accomplished in another's continuum' as a standard phrase — here as the refuge of those who seek only higher rebirth — which shows how old the wording the opponent relies on is.

quotes.text: འདོད་ན། སྟོན་པ་ཤཱཀྱ་ཐུབ་པ་ཆོས་ཅན། རྒྱུ་སྐྱབས་མ་ཡིན་པར་ཐལ། འབྲས་སྐྱབས་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར། དེར་ཐལ། ཁྱེའུ་སྣང་བྱེད་དང་ང་ལས་ནུའི་འབྲས་སྐྱབས་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར། དེ་གཉིས་ཀྱི་ཐོབ་བྱ་མཐར་ཐུག་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར། འདོད་མི་ནུས་ཏེ། རང་གི་གདུལ་བྱ་ཐེག་པ་གསུམ་གྱི་གང་ཟག་གི་རྒྱུ་སྐྱབས་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར།
quotes.why: Jamyang Zhepa (Gomang) using the same stock examples — Śākyamuni as result refuge of his own former lives and cause refuge of his disciples — to show that cause refuge and result refuge are not incompatible; he makes the point by cases, not through the 'one continuum' relation.

quotes.citation: འགྲེལ་པ་དོན་གསལ། on the ten instructions, the instruction on the Three Jewels
quotes.why: Haribhadra's gloss on the lemma: the instruction on the Buddha Jewel is to know it without apprehending it; he says nothing about cause and result refuges or about whose continuum a Jewel belongs to.
The root-text line on which the yig cha hangs its whole refuge excursus.
